headline: Ramaphosa Fights His Own Impeachment's Prosecutor
script: This is history in the making — for the first time ever, a sitting SA president faces impeachment, over the Phala Phala scandal where hundreds of thousands of dollars vanished from his farm couch. Parliament's committee voted 9-7 to pick Advocate Thandazani Madonsela as the evidence leader — basically the person leading the case against Ramaphosa. But Ramaphosa just formally objected, saying Madonsela's got conflicts of interest, including past ANC legal work. Opposition parties aren't buying it. EFF's Julius Malema said, quote, 'he is not going to choose his own judge.' ActionSA says he's dodging accountability. The committee's now getting a legal opinion instead of moving forward. Why care? This is the president under investigation trying to shape who investigates him — months before you vote in the November municipal elections. Watch this space.
why_it_matters: It's a real-time test of whether South Africa's most powerful person can be held accountable by the same rules as everyone else, right before young voters head to the polls.
